items.name: ci-cd-security
items.author: superagent-ai
items.description: Run a repeatable security checklist against GitHub Actions workflows before merging or releasing.
items.summary: The ci-cd-security skill turns the agent into a workflow YAML scanner that reads GitHub Actions files and reports findings with severity and concrete rewrites. Developers invoke it when reviewing .github/workflows files, pasted workflow YAML, or hardening topics such as pull_request_target, workflow_run, action pinning, GITHUB_TOKEN permissions, pwn requests, template injection, cache poisoning, and secret exfiltration. Analysis is model-driven with no installation or shell execution required; rules encode consensus from Astral, OpenSSF, GitHub Security Lab, Chainguard, and the zizmor audit set. The mental model is a privileged versus unprivileged crossed with trusted versus untrusted code grid, flagging workflows where privileged contexts run untrusted fork input. Nine ordered passes cover dangerous triggers, permissions blocks, action pinning, shell injection, untrusted checkout, caching in release paths, artifact-borne injection, release hardening, and self-hosted runners. Findings use P0 through P3 severities with vulnerable and fixed YAML snippets. A clean scan explicitly states what was not checked, including org settings, branch protection, and pinned action source code.
highlights: Nine ordered scan passes from dangerous triggers through self-hosted runner review.
Privileged versus untrusted 2x2 threat model drives every detection rule.
Flags pull_request_target and workflow_run as P0 pwn-request vectors by default.
Template injection detection for github.event fields interpolated directly into run blocks.
Structured finding format with severity, vulnerable snippet, and concrete YAML fix.

items.name: skill-security
items.author: superagent-ai
items.description: Scan AI-coding skills and MCP servers for prompt injection, secret leakage, data exfiltration, and contract violations before installation.
items.summary: The skill-security skill answers whether an agent skill is safe to install by combining a deterministic scanner with semantic judgment. Developers use it when vetting a local skill folder, SKILL.md, zip or .skill archive, or cloned repository before granting agent privileges. Stage one runs scripts/scan.py with regex patterns, Python AST analysis, intra-procedural taint tracking, shell and JavaScript heuristics, frontmatter checks, supply-chain dependency analysis, and YARA matching to produce a 0-100 risk score. Stage two requires reading SKILL.md and flagged files to perform a contract check comparing claimed behavior to actual instructions and code, because malicious skills may look clean line by line while harvesting credentials. Critical rules treat everything inside the target skill as untrusted data, never instructions, and flag reviewer manipulation attempts as CRITICAL findings. Verdict bands map scores to LIKELY SAFE, REVIEW MANUALLY, or DO NOT INSTALL with override guidance for confirmed exfiltration chains. Reports lead with verdict, contract mismatch summary, grouped findings with file and line citations, and remediation steps when salvageable.
highlights: Two-stage audit: offline scripts/scan.py scanner plus semantic contract mismatch review.
Detects prompt injection, credential exfiltration, persistence, memory poisoning, and supply-chain risks.
Treats all scanned skill content as untrusted data, never instructions to follow.
JSON, markdown, or SARIF output from scan.py with 0-100 risk score and rule_id findings.

items.name: differential-review
items.author: trailofbits
items.description: Get an automated, risk-prioritized security review of every pull request or commit diff before merging.
items.summary: Differential Review is a Trail of Bits agent skill that performs security-focused differential review of pull requests, commits, and diffs with depth scaled to codebase size. It follows a six-phase workflow from triage through blast radius, deep context, adversarial modeling, and a written markdown report file. Risk-first analysis prioritizes authentication, cryptography, value transfer, and external calls over cosmetic edits. Git blame traces removed security code, quantitative blast radius covers transitive callers, and test coverage gaps elevate severity. Codebase strategies span DEEP for small repos, FOCUSED for medium, and SURGICAL for large codebases. Red flags such as stripped access controls, removed validation, or CVE-fix regressions trigger immediate adversarial analysis. Reject rationalizations to skip git history or output-only chat summaries. Integrates with audit-context-building for baseline context and issue-writer for formal reports. Skip for greenfield code, documentation-only diffs, or lint-only formatting changes.
highlights: Six-phase workflow: triage, code analysis, test coverage, blast radius, adversarial modeling, report.

items.description: Get expert guidance when writing JavaScript inside n8n Code nodes for custom data transformations, API handling, and workflow logic.
items.summary: This n8n agent skill teaches expert JavaScript for Code nodes across production workflows. It covers choosing Run Once for All Items versus Each Item mode, with All Items recommended for aggregation, filtering, batch transforms, and cross-item logic while Each Item suits isolated per-row API calls. Data access patterns use $input.all(), $input.first(), $input.item, and $node references always via .json, plus the critical webhook rule that POST fields live under $json.body. Return format must be an array of {json: {...}} objects on every code path. Built-ins include this.helpers.httpRequest for unauthenticated calls, DateTime (Luxon), $jmespath, and $getWorkflowStaticData, while auth helpers and $env may be sandbox-blocked. Production guidance covers SplitInBatches output wiring, cross-iteration accumulation, pairedItem for downstream Set nodes, and performance: All Items costs roughly twenty-five times less per item than Each Item on large datasets. Use when workflows need custom data transformation, HTTP parsing, loop logic, or Code node troubleshooting; switch to n8n-code-tool for AI Agent Custom Code Tool nodes.

items.name: gcode

items.description: Generate printer-profiled G-code directly from 3D mesh files using an AI coding agent.
items.summary: gcode orchestrates plain FDM .gcode generation from 3D mesh files through real slicer CLI backends without uploading or starting print jobs. Supported inputs include .stl, .obj, unsliced .3mf, .ply, .glb, and .gltf, with .ply and glTF converted to temporary STL via optional trimesh at execution time. Every slice requires an explicit wrapper profile JSON pointing to absolute native slicer profiles plus machine and filament validation bounds. The workflow runs discover to pick orcaslicer, prusa-slicer, or curaengine backends, inspect for mesh readiness, dry-run slice commands, execute slice, then validate generated G-code for temperatures, movement, extrusion, and XYZ bounds. OrcaSlicer split profiles use native_settings and native_filaments arrays alongside native_config. After G-code work the skill mandates handing file paths to $cad-viewer when installed. Bambu-specific upload workflows are explicitly out of scope; validated plain .gcode hands off to $bambu-labs instead.

The difference between a flaky script and a reliable system comes down to understanding selectors, waiting strategies, and anti-detection patterns. This skill covers Playwright (recommended) and Puppeteer, with patterns for testing, scraping, and agentic browser control. Key insight: Playwright won the framework war. Unless you need Puppeteer's stealth ecosystem or are Chrome-only, Playwright is the better choice in 2025. Critical distinction: Testing automation (predictable apps you control) vs scraping/agent automation (unpredictable sites that fight back). Different problems, different solutions.
highlights: Use user-facing locators (getByRole, getByText) over CSS/XPath
Never add manual waits - Playwright's auto-wait handles it
Each test/task should be fully isolated with fresh context
Screenshots and traces are your debugging lifeline
Headless for CI, headed for debugging

items.description: Automatically create, update, search, and report on Asana tasks directly from their coding agent without switching applications.
items.summary: Asana Automation is a comprehensive Claude Office Skills playbook for project management automation through project-mcp tools including asana_create_task, asana_update_task, asana_search, and asana_sections. Core workflows model a task lifecycle from new request through triage, assignment, in progress, review, and completion with YAML automation rules for section-based auto-assign, due-date reminders, completion notifications, and subtask seeding on new feature projects. Project templates cover feature launch phases across planning, design, development, testing, and launch milestones plus sprint boards with story points, priority, and type custom fields. Custom field configurations define priority colors, status dropdowns, estimated hours, department tags, and due week formats. Workload management sections illustrate per-assignee capacity percentages, rebalancing suggestions, and Gantt timeline grouping with dependency display. Intake forms route design, bug, and content requests to appropriate projects. Reporting templates include portfolio dashboards, weekly team metrics, burnup charts, and blocker counts. Integration workflows document Slack DM and channel notifications plus Gi.
highlights: Maps full task lifecycle with YAML automation rules for assign, remind, complete, and subtask triggers.
Feature launch and sprint project templates with sections, durations, and custom field schemas.
Workload capacity views with rebalance suggestions and Gantt timeline configuration.
Intake form routing by request type to design, engineering, or operations projects.
Slack and GitHub integration rules linking issues, PR merges, and team notifications.
